about: The [[wikilink]] and ![[embed]] targets in a note's text, in order, as written: without a #heading, ^block or |alias, trimmed. Empty targets are left out. Markdown [text](path) links are not in this file.
typescript: wikilinkTargets in src/shell/linksTags.ts (the Outgoing links view)
rust: parse_note in src-tauri/src/index/parse.rs: the targets of its links that are not markdown links

cases.name: ^ without #
cases.note: Obsidian's Link to blocks help page documents block references as [[Note#^block]], always with #. Without #, ^ is part of the target name (inference from Obsidian Help: Internal links / Link to blocks).

cases.name: a [ inside the target
cases.note: Inference: [ is allowed inside a [[...]] target, consistent with TS and triple brackets [[[Note]]]; unverified in Obsidian Help.

cases.name: escaped pipe in a table cell
cases.note: Obsidian Help (Tables / Internal links): inside a table, \| escapes the pipe in [[Note\|alias]] so the table cell does not split and the link target is Note.

cases.name: unclosed fence runs to the end
the other marker closes a fence (TS)
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets toggles on any fence line, so ``` closes the ~~~ block and [[B]] ends up inside a new one. Rust (and CommonMark, so likely Obsidian) only closes on the same marker. tagsInText's fence rule also agrees with Rust (see tags.json).

cases.name: a shorter fence closes a longer one (TS)
cases.note: As above: TS's wikilinkTargets ignores fence length. Rust and CommonMark need a closing fence at least as long.

cases.name: fence indented with a tab
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets allows any spaces or tabs before a fence; Rust allows up to 3 whitespace characters, tabs included. Both open a fence here. In CommonMark a tab is 4 columns, so this is an indented code line and not a fence; tagsInText agrees with that (see tags.json).

cases.name: fence indented 4 spaces
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets opens a fence at any indent. Rust, tagsInText and CommonMark allow at most 3 spaces, so this is not a fence.

cases.name: closing fence indented 4 spaces
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets and Rust's fence_close both close at any indent. tagsInText and CommonMark need at most 3 spaces, so the block runs to the end.

cases.name: closing fence with text after it
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets closes on any line starting with ```. Rust, tagsInText and CommonMark do not close on a fence line with text after it.

cases.name: a backtick in a backtick fence's info string
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets opens a fence on any line starting with ```. Rust, tagsInText and CommonMark: a backtick in the info string means it is not a fence.

cases.name: inline code
cases.note: TS's wikilinkTargets does not skip inline code. CONTRACT.md says links in inline code are skipped, and Rust does that. TS is likely wrong here.

cases.name: double-backtick inline code
cases.note: Rust blanks CommonMark code spans (any run length). TS's wikilinkTargets does not skip inline code at all.

cases.name: heading, block and alias
cases.note: The file target drops the heading, the block and the alias. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: embed display width
cases.note: The pipe sets a width, not a different file. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: md extension stays in the raw target
cases.note: The raw target keeps .md, the heading and the alias aside. Obsidian's resolver later treats a .md target as that note. This list is the raw target.

cases.name: spaces and case stay in the raw target
cases.note: Spaces inside the name stay, and so does case. Obsidian resolves two casings to one file, which is a later step than this list.

cases.name: a percent-encoded wikilink stays encoded
cases.note: A wikilink is not percent-decoded. Obsidian keeps this text as the target.

cases.name: an encoded markdown link is not a wikilink
cases.note: There is no wikilink here. Obsidian's markdown-link index does include these targets, decoded and without the heading. That index is not this function, so there is no obsidian override.

cases.name: a backslash before the opening brackets
cases.note: Obsidian treats the backslash as an escape, so the first pair is text. TS and Rust both still see [[.

cases.name: triple brackets
cases.note: Inference: the outer [[ closes at ]] and keeps the inner [ in the target ([Note), consistent with TS.

cases.name: an escaped bracket inside the target
cases.note: Inference: [ is allowed in a target and \ is kept as written (unlike \|); unverified in Obsidian Help.

cases.name: a link in an indented code block
cases.note: Four spaces after a blank line is an indented code block. Obsidian's reading view and its link index skip the link inside it. TS and Rust have no indented-code rule, so both return Inside.

cases.name: a link inside an HTML comment
cases.note: Obsidian does not put a link inside <!-- --> into the graph or the backlinks. TS and Rust both keep Secret.

cases.name: a link inside a %% comment
cases.note: Reading view hides the comment. The metadata cache still indexes the link (a rename updates it). Both runners return both targets. Obsidian agrees with this list.

cases.name: percent signs inside the target
cases.note: The cache's target is the whole text, Note%%draft. The editor may style %% as a comment, but the link target does not stop there. Both runners agree.

cases.name: a same-note heading has an empty file target
cases.note: Obsidian does treat these as links, to a heading or block of the current note. The file target is empty, and this list leaves empty targets out. Both runners agree.

cases.name: links written next to each other
cases.note: No space is required between them. Obsidian agrees.

cases.name: an escaped pipe outside a table
cases.note: Inference from Obsidian Help's table pipe escape ([[Note\|alias]]): \| is normalized to | as the alias separator everywhere, so the target is Note.

cases.name: an embed inside inline code
cases.note: Same gap as the inline-code case: TS's wikilinkTargets does not skip inline code, so the embed counts. Rust and Obsidian skip it.
